title: Deterministic offline upgrade contract and network guardrails for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines a deterministic contract for offline (zero or minimal egress) upgrades in Private/VPC deployments. Goal: provide a prescriptive acceptance checklist and operational guardrails that site operators and customers can use to validate upgrade readiness and to run safe, repeatable staged rollouts in environments with restricted network egress, custom proxies, or airgap constraints. The PRD clarifies required preflight checks, artifact provenance, KMS rotation behavior, operator rollback triggers, and quantitative validation tests (bandwidth emulation, partition simulation, checksum reconciliation).
acceptance_criteria: Preflight checklist: node time sync, disk pressure < 70%, operator permissions verified, required ports open on control plane egress whitelist
Artifact provenance: all images must be signed and verifiable via customer mirror; checksum reconciliation must be demonstrated in a simulated mirror run
Zero-egress mode support: upgrades succeed when only allowed mirror endpoint and KMS endpoints are reachable (configurable allowlist); show a successful staged install in isolated test cluster
Staged rollout contract: canary percentage, wait windows, health probe thresholds, automatic rollback triggers documented and configured (e.g., 5% canary / 30m / <95% readiness triggers rollback)
Operatorless bootstrap fallback: if the operator cannot pull artifacts, control plane must provide human-readable failure codes and remediation hints in logs and runbook
KMS rotation compatibility: in-airgap KMS proxy or offline-wrapped keys must allow node-level certificate renewal without internet egress; test procedure documented
Bandwidth-sim acceptance: upgrade completes within acceptable time when mirror bandwidth is throttled to X Mbps (test matrix attached); percent-complete telemetry reported
Partition tolerance: simulated network partition during upgrade must result in safe quiesce or deterministic rollback with no data corruption (validated via test harness)
Telemetry & audit: upgrade events must be emitted to local audit logs and to optional mirrored telemetry endpoint; sample log snippets and retention policy provided
Runbook & automated remediation: clear runbook with rollback commands, partial-fix steps and postmortem checklist included; runbook reviewed by SRE and PM
decisions: Require signed images by default; customer mirror may host signed artifacts. We will not ship unsigned artifact fallback.
Adopt a minimal allowed egress matrix (mirror + KMS + optional licensing endpoint). Any additional egress must be negotiated per-customer as an exception.
Use operator-exit codes as a standard remediation signal; documented mapping between exit codes and runbook steps.
Canary policy: opt-in default of progressive percentage with configurable safety windows; must support manual override by operator.
Testing harness: re-use existing private-deploy test harness but extend for bandwidth and partition simulation scenarios.
followups: ENG: implement image-signing verifier and local checksum reconcile command (ENG-1842)
